definition: The task of automatically translating text from one natural language into another.
details: Machine translation was one of the earliest and most impactful applications of neural sequence-to-sequence models, and the encoder-decoder attention mechanisms developed for translation directly inspired the transformer architecture.

explainer.lead: Machine translation automatically converts text from one natural language to another, one of the earliest and most impactful uses of neural sequence-to-sequence models. The encoder-decoder attention mechanisms developed for translation directly inspired the transformer architecture.

tiers.eli5: It's like having a tireless interpreter who reads a sentence in one language and types it out in another.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train encoder-decoder or transformer models to map a source sentence to a target sentence; a common pitfall is that attention learned for translation gets reused everywhere, so it's easy to forget domain adaptation still matters.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a sequence-to-sequence model learns P(y|x) where x is the source sentence and y the target; encoder-decoder attention was developed for this task and led to the transformer.

explainer.example: A model reads the English sentence 'the cat sat' and outputs the French 'le chat s'est assis'.
